name: viewer
title: Viewer
description: The skeleton of a thing open in a panel, e.g. a file: a toolbar above of islands with no line under them, the path's and one per group of tools (ViewerTools, each ViewerToolGroup an island of its own: a pill 36px high on the page's colour with a hairline and a faint shadow, a step lighter than the panel in dark, its buttons 28px; a lone tool a round island) (the path's folders folded into a menu where they have no room, the path on a row of its own over the tools where its name would be cut short of 6rem, a name cut keeping its extension) (back, its path as a breadcrumb or the app's start in their place, none where a tab names it, its own tools, the app's, add to chat, download, a menu of the app's), its content to the edges, and a status bar below (controls at the start, facts at the end), or an action bar (ViewerActionBar: what the actions act on, small, then the app's buttons, e.g. Discard and Commit); a frame whose toolbar would hold its path alone may go without one. Its parts compose any viewer; ViewerFrame lays them out from props, ViewerFrame is one row above in a panel and over the window alike (its path or `start`, the kind's own `lead` such as compare; its `zoom`, tools, the app's actions, add to chat, download, More with its facts at the top where the kind has no status bar, `statusBar={false}`), the content to the edges, and a floating bar of ways to change it at the content's foot (ViewerEditBar: a handle to drag it aside by, the kind's own such as an image's marking, then the app's `edits`, ViewerEditButton's icon and word, the icon alone where the viewer is under 24rem; gone with none). ViewerZoom is a toolbar's percent (a menu of Fit, in, out and the steps) or a status bar's zoom with Fit (its value a menu of the steps and Fit; in and out a step at least a fifth larger or smaller, so one from a fitted size is never a few percent), ViewerFrameEnd gives a frame's surroundings tools at the end of its toolbar (as ViewerOverlay's close), ViewerFrameTitlebar makes its toolbar the window's top row (as ViewerOverlay's: as tall as an AgentApp's titlebar, past the window's own buttons or --viewer-titlebar-start, dragging the window but by its controls; its name, its facts after it, quieter, not in More, then lead, the surroundings' tools at its end) and its tools islands under the content, as a photo app's (ways to change it, in place of the floating bar, then the zoom, tools, actions, add to chat, download and More; on two rows where they have no room on one), ViewerMenu a tool that opens a menu (More, or one of its own icon, as wide as its items), ViewerFilter a filter of its bars, ViewerFind a find bar (floating over the content, or a bar's field) with its count and the previous and next match, and ViewerUnsupported says a file has no preview. Buttons named by tooltips, a finger's place on touch screens. ViewerFrame takes position ({ index, count }), onPrevious and onNext for the app's others: round buttons by the content's sides (none at the ends) and "3 / 7" at its foot (labels.previous, next, among); ViewerSiblings draws them over any relative content.
